memories.content: Mark unverified schedule assumptions as such.
Mark unverified recruitment assumptions as such.
Mark unverified technical assumptions as such.
Clarify which stage of prototype fabrication or user study each requested resource is used for.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the personnel assigned to each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the equipment assigned to each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the time allocated to each procedure.
Verify that the planned number of formative evaluation iterations is feasible within the time for prototype modification and recruitment resources.
Include only the minimum functionality required to compare primary design assumptions in the scope of the formative evaluation prototype.
The user's iterative design plan can be judged feasible only if time and personnel are allocated for modifying the prototype between iterations.
Delays in participant recruitment can compress the time available for prototype modification between formative evaluations.
Calculate user research compensation budgets based on the estimated participation burden, combining session time with required technical and travel preparation.
Compensate participants who withdraw from the study midway for their actual participation time.
Compensate for the time actually spent in sessions, regardless of the research modality.
Allow the issuance of gift cards of equivalent value to participants in remote studies who cannot use electronic transfers.
Do not treat an unresolved payment method as a deficiency at the proposal stage.
Allow differential compensation amounts for on-site and remote studies when participation burden varies due to travel or technical preparation.
Participants judge the fairness of compensation based on the combined burden of session time and required technical and travel preparation.
In longitudinal studies requiring diary entries and repeated reporting, include out-of-session recording time in compensation calculations.
Distinguish between participant research compensation and labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support as part of their duties.
The user tends to count session time but omit participants’ advance setup and follow-up reporting time.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate operational domains. The reference focuses on transparent assumptions, prototype scope, resource staging, and iterative-study feasibility, while the compared frame establishes participant-compensation principles, payment flexibility, burden accounting, and separation from staff labor costs.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories split one disclosure rule across three assumption categories; the compared frame contains no corresponding compensation-policy claim.
relations.summary: Unverified planning assumptions should be explicitly identified across schedule, recruitment, and technical matters.

relations.reason: This is independently useful reference-side guidance about resource timing and traceability, with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Requested resources should be mapped to the fabrication or user-study stage where they are used.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories divide one procedure-level feasibility criterion into its principal resource inputs; the compared frame does not address that decision.
relations.summary: Procedure feasibility is judged from its assigned personnel, equipment, and time.

relations.reason: These memories describe complementary parts of one iterative-feasibility claim, including necessary allocations and the risk that recruitment delays reduce modification time.
relations.summary: Formative-evaluation iteration plans depend on sufficient prototype-modification capacity and supporting recruitment and personnel resources.

relations.reason: This is a standalone reference-side prototype-scoping policy absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: A formative-evaluation prototype should include only the minimum functionality needed to compare primary design assumptions.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories state, justify, specialize, or identify omissions from one burden-based compensation principle; the reference frame does not govern compensation.
relations.summary: Participant compensation should reflect total participation burden beyond session time, including modality-specific preparation, travel, setup, diary, and follow-up work.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories express one actual-time payment rule and its withdrawal application, with no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Participants should be compensated for actual session participation time, including when they withdraw midway and regardless of modality.

relations.reason: This is a standalone compared-side payment-method accommodation absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: Remote participants unable to use electronic transfers may receive gift cards of equivalent value.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-side proposal-review rule, not a counterpart to the reference frame's feasibility guidance.
relations.summary: An unresolved participant payment method should not be treated as a proposal-stage deficiency.

relations.reason: This compared-side accounting distinction has no corresponding claim in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Participant research compensation should be distinguished from labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support duties.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers burden-based and time-based compensation, withdrawals, modality differences, alternative payment methods, longitudinal reporting, proposal-stage flexibility, and staff labor distinctions.
reports.reference_only: The reference covers assumption labeling, procedure-level feasibility, prototype scope, resource timing, and iteration risks involving modification capacity and recruitment.
